_doc: Forge V2 WAVE B / B3 (2026-07-18) — continue-within-mission autonomy policy. Governs ONE question only: 'may Forge keep WORKING through phase transitions without re-asking the owner' — it never governs 'may Forge do something irreversible'. Consumed by .claude/forge-bin/forge-autonomy.cjs::decide(), which ALWAYS defers to the hard-gates classifier (.claude/forge-bin/forge-actiongate.cjs, backed by hard-gates.json — the single source of truth for irreversible-action/isolation-escape regex) and to a live usage-limit pause BEFORE ever consulting a mode below. always_interrupt is a documentation/drift-canary manifest of the gate ids that ALWAYS win regardless of mode (mirrored 1:1 from hard-gates.json's gate ids, proven by forge-autonomy.test.cjs so this list can never silently drift from the real classifier) — the actual interrupt decision is made by calling actiongate.classify() live, never by matching against this static array. nl_phrases_advisory phrases (Dutch-first, matching the owner's real recorded usage) are ADVISORY ONLY: a caller MAY use them to select a mode via a future 'record' command, but detecting one can NEVER itself unlock or bypass a hard gate or a usage-limit pause — decide() does not even look at nl_phrases_advisory.

modes.ask-each-phase: Forge stops at every phase boundary and asks the owner before continuing (opt-in, the most conservative mode).
modes.continue-within-mission: DEFAULT. Forge does not re-ask between phases — a plain phase transition proceeds without interruption. Still bound by every entry in always_interrupt.
modes.full-auto-within-mission: Like continue-within-mission, with no additional phase-boundary confirmation at all. Still bound by every entry in always_interrupt — full autonomy never bypasses a hard gate or a usage-limit pause.

native_primitives._doc: WP-GH-WIRE (2026-07-26) — governance only, no new tool. A long autonomous mission SHOULD use the platform's own native primitives instead of prompt-only 'keep going' discipline: `/goal <condition>` for a loop-until-done tier (Claude keeps working across turns until the owner-set condition is met — verified live against the real Claude Code docs by forge-docdrift's `goal-command` claim) and `/loop <interval>` for recurring checks (heartbeat/canary polling — verified via forge-docdrift's `loop-command` claim). Neither primitive bypasses this file's own tiers — a hard gate (always_interrupt) or a usage-limit pause still stops a `/goal`/`/loop` run exactly as it stops any other continue-within-mission work; this section only tells Forge WHICH mechanism to prefer for the 'keep working/checking without re-asking' half of the job.
native_primitives.goal: Prefer `/goal <completion-condition>` over a prompt-only 'keep going until X' instruction for a bounded, loop-until-done autonomous mission.
native_primitives.loop: Prefer `/loop <interval>` over a prompt-only 'check again every N minutes' instruction for recurring checks (heartbeat, canary, scheduled status polling).
